newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Former Estate Mortgage auditors settle - Meridian.
newsitem.headline: Former Estate Mortgage auditors settle - Meridian.

text.p: Former Estate Mortgage trust, Meridian Investment Trust, said on Wednesday former Estate Mortgage auditors Priestley & Morris had agreed to pay A$31 million in an out-of-court settlement.

The settlement covered all claims between the trustees and the auditors in the ongoing trial relating to the A$600 million collapse of investment group Estate Mortgage in 1990, Meridian said in a statement.
"By settling now we are also shortening the length of the trial by about two months resulting in subsrtantial savings in legal costs," Meridian trustee John Murphy said in a statement.
About 21 percent of the settlement funds less costs would be paid to Meridian's lenders, Mediuan said.

Meridian and its managers Tyndall Funds Management ltd are pitted against defendants, including food ingredients group Burns Philp & Co Ltd in the Estate Mortgage case which began in early February and WAs expected to run for up to 12 months.

According to defence documents prepared by Burns Philp, its subsidiary Burns Philp Trustee Co (BPTC) was the Estate Mortgage trustee from 1983 until it went into liquidation during a cash crisis in 1990.
Meridian trustees Murphy and Peter Allen of Arthur Andersen were seeking to prove Burns Philp was a "shadow director of BPTC and therefore liable for losses suffered in relation to 13 mortgage loans.
At 0245 GMT (12.45 p.m.) Meridian shares were 14 cents firmer at A$1.35.
